0.name: Parks Inspection Program — Inspections
0.note: The window above must match PIP_SINCE_YEAR in parks_validation.py. The only source that GRADES the park itself. A rating is A for acceptable and U for unacceptable. This entry serves 2 export rows: `cleanliness` becomes `pip_acceptable_rate` and `overall_condition` becomes `pip_condition_acceptable_rate`. The 2 are different visual constructs — the surface today against the fabric — and version 1.1.0 exported only the first. 151,484 inspections in total, about 6,500 each year, so filter the year on the server. PIP inspects a ZONE and names it B007-01; cut the suffix to reach the parent property B007. WARNING: on 2026-08-31 this source serves 0 rows through the API. Both metrics come from the disk cache that a 2026-08-12 pull filled. Do not delete notebooks/cvpr/.proxy_cache/.

1.name: DPR Parks Properties
1.note: 2,059 sites with shapes. FacDB carries no prop_id, so the proxy reaches a geography on its own, the same way the schools case uses the DOE point file. After the zone rollup, 1,428 of 2,406 PIP sites match a shape (59.4%), and those carry 83.1% of all inspections. Of the 978 misses, 974 use a non-standard id (BT## tree districts, BR borough-wide, _temp) and are not discrete parks; only 4 are true property ids.

2.name: ACS 5-Year 2024, table S1901 — median household income by census tract
2.note: An area proxy. It describes the households around a park, not the park. Only the census-tract layer carries a true median.

3.name: NYPD complaints, 2026 Q1, pulled 2026-06-29
3.note: An area proxy. Crime is point data, so every layer gets a true value. WARNING: the file name says year to date, but the record stops on 2026-03-31. 94.8% of the 133,114 complaints fall in January to March 2026, and the rest are late reports of older events. Read this source as 1 winter quarter, never as a full year.

4.name: DPR Parks Properties — acquisition date
4.note: The vintage of a park. A park is land, not a building, thus it carries no construction year: only 33% of the park units hold a BIN at all, and that BIN is a comfort station or a recreation building. The acquisition date is the year the land became a park. 1,972 of 2,059 properties carry one, and the units reach 93.6% through the same spatial join that PIP uses. WARNING: acquisition is not construction — a park acquired in 1936 can hold a playground of 2015. WARNING: a year is not oriented.

5.name: DPR Parks Properties — acreage
5.note: The SIZE of a park. All 2,059 properties carry a value: the median is 0.70 acres and the largest is 2,772 acres. The value rides on the same DPR point layer that PIP and the acquisition year ride on, thus a park lands in the polygon its rating lands in. WARNING: acreage is not oriented and it is not a quality measure. A positive correlation says that the model calls a LARGER park better. Why it belongs here: a photograph of a large park shows a horizon and a tree line, and a photograph of a small one shows a fence and a building, so the model can read size without reading upkeep. Measured 2026-08-31 at the park unit, gemma-4-12b reaches rho +0.285 against acreage and -0.023 against the cleanliness rate.

6.name: Parks Inspection Program — Feature Ratings
6.note: A per-feature A or U rating, 1,408,115 rows. It rates exactly the parts of a park that a photograph shows: Benches 93,678, Paved Surfaces 125,484, Sidewalks 110,415, Play Equipment 65,631, Fences 99,745, Safety Surface 50,854, Trails 8,680. A feature rate would be the structural companion of the cleanliness rate. WARNING: the source carries NO prop_id. Its only key is the inspection id, and the Inspections source (entry 0) returns 0 rows through the API today, thus a feature rating cannot reach a park. No other PIP table maps an inspection id to a property: the Inventory (86a8-pqby) holds prop_id and feature but no rating, and Conditions & Hazards (ibip-ftv5), Element Tracking (2jvr-j6ne), PIP Plus (uisg-ivwv), and Daily Immediate Attentions (s6dm-mdan) hold no prop_id. Build the rate when the Inspections source serves rows again. `_proxies_parks.pip_feature_status()` tests this on every run.
